cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Dactylic hexameter is the metre of epic poetry: six feet per line, each foot being a dactyl (- uu) or spondee (--). The final foot is always a spondee or trochee.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: A dactyl is one long syllable followed by two short syllables (dum-di-di). A spondee is two long syllables (dum-dum).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: The caesura is a natural pause within a hexameter line, usually in the third foot, creating rhythm and structure.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Elision occurs when a word ending in a vowel runs into a word beginning with a vowel or h-: the final vowel is not pronounced separately.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Enjambement is when a sentence runs over from one line to the next without a pause, creating momentum and suspense.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Alliteration is the repetition of initial consonant sounds for emphasis or onomatopoeic effect.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Onomatopoeia uses words that imitate sounds: Virgil's 'sternitur' mimics a body striking the ground.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Poetic vocabulary differs from prose: poets use archaic words, Greek forms, and extended meanings.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Hyperbaton (separating adjective from noun) is used extensively in poetry for emphasis, beauty, and sound.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Poetic Metre & Style
cards.back: Sound effects: assonance (repeated vowels), consonance (repeated consonants), and homoeoteleuton (similar endings) all contribute to musical quality.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse latin exam tips — poetic metre & style?
cards.back: 1. For Poetic Metre & Style, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Poetic Metre & Style, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
